Hard mode, huh? You, I like.
Here, have pain.

A memory that seems like fiction now.
It must have been weeks since mother nature decided to evaporate our lives.
Family, friends, sons, daughters — they all wait for us now in the great beyond.
We could not take everyone, and we had to make many hard choices on who would get a chance to live.
We cut loose the sick so the kids could live
[[C]]The oldest adults are left behind. [[+]]+{I1} [[icon:UI/images/game/ico-child]] Child Beaver [[-]]-{I2} Adult Beaver
They tried to take as many with us as we could
[[C]]Pay [[good:{S1}:{I3}]] and [[good:{S2}:{I3}]] in [[time:{F1}d]]. [[+]]+{I1} [[icon:UI/images/game/ico-child]] Child Beaver. Two adults become contaminated.
There was only so much we could do
Kids don't build a city. Engineers and labourers do
{0} was left behind on the great trek.
The colony is worn down by the trek.

Failure...
I was meant to save them, but I led them all to their doom...
[[C]]There is no colony left to lead. [[-]]{%4} life expectancy for [[time:{F5}d]]
The weight of those left behind.

As the day comes to an end you spot two kits hugging and crying.
With their grandfather abandoned during the great trek, Marius and Melissa are now alone in this cold world.
When Marius notices you he starts shouting, calling you names like monster and murderer.
In his crying fit of rage he throws something at you: a small necklace with the picture of an old man on it.
Marius then took Melissa by her paw and ran away.
I did what I had to...

As the day comes to an end you spot an old man with two kits.
Upon noticing you the old man gives you a laboured smile and stumbles over.
"Thank you for saving us. I am the only family these kits have left.
I know I'm useless with my hands, but I used to be a factory foreman.
Let me help you get your bearings. Oh, and take this — please light it on the day we are saved."
He turns back to the kits, who are smiling with youthful energy, and you are left with a firework in your hands.
The old factory foreman helps the colony find its bearings.

As the day comes to an end you lie down in your tent and think back on the many hard decisions you had to make.
One vision haunts your dreams: an old man hugging what looked like his grandchildren.
You doomed them. Sent them to their deaths. Refused their chance of living.
Many don't sleep that night and awake tired.
I am a monster made out of necessity
A haunted night leaves the colony slow and tired.

As the day comes to an end you lie down in your tent, only to get woken by screaming.
Outside, two beavers are going fist to fist after a heated debate about their abandoned kits.
They're workers tired from labour and travel, and they decided to "indulge" themselves.
You confiscate the goods and go to bed late. Many wake up tired. The tension will be noticeable for days.
[[C]][[+]]+[[good:{S1}:{I1}]] [[-]]Two beavers are injured. {%1} working speed for [[time:{F2}d]]. {I2} science
The fight over abandoned kits leaves the workforce strained.

Melissa walks into your room with paperwork.
"It is done, Captain. Soon we will be filling the lands with new life, and it's all thanks to you!"
Your chair creaks as you get up and take a firework rocket from the cupboard.
"Your grandfather gave me this when you were young."
I say it's time we light it

"Please light it on the day we are saved."
The old man's words are still fresh as Marius, his grandson, lights the firework rocket.
You would have done it yourself, but you too are showing your age, and kneeling is nearly impossible.
The rocket shoots up. After all the sacrifices it took to get this far, it explodes into a picture of your face — just a bit younger.
You can't help but chuckle.

Your builders approach with two plans to power the aquifer.
The first, and most favorable, is a power wheel. Fast, straightforward, every beaver already knows what to do. It would need at least two beavers operating it at all times.
The second is some alternative source — geothermals or waterwheels. That means planning, rationing, and a lot of downsides.
Build the power wheel. Let's get this done
[[C]][[+]]{%1} working speed and {%2} movement speed for [[time:{F3}d]]
My plans are beyond your understanding
[[C]]Pay [[good:{S4}:{I3}]] in [[time:{F3}d]]. [[+]]+[[good:{S3}:{I1}]] +[[good:Science:{I2}]] {%6} movement speed [[-]]{%4} working speed for [[time:{F5}d]]
The colony knows this work and moves quickly.
Rationing and planning slow the work, but the colony covers more ground.

{CP_Speaker_Name} grumbles as she goes to work. Water rationing is taking effect.
She and her daughter will only get half the water they need. The rest will be berry juice.
It's nutritious, but it's just not very good for the teeth.
[[C]][[+]]{%1} working speed for [[time:{F2}d]] +[[good:{S2}:{I1}]] [[-]]Three beavers get chipped teeth
The colony works harder on thinner water.

Your childhood friend — probably the only person left alive you still care for — was pregnant.
She told no one. Now she is recovering from giving birth.
She asked you to bless the child. Exhausted, she smiles as you walk in.
"I'm naming her after your mother."
"After my mother?"
"Your mother was always there for me when I needed help. The same could not be said about my own parents."
The room is quiet. "So you're calling her—"
"Lily," she says.
You look at the small bright eyes of the kit.

A drought is approaching fast, and beavers are getting nervous.
It's about time you said something to ease their minds — hopefully.
You step onto the makeshift stand.
"My fellow survivors."
Our progress shall be grand. All will get something to drink
Lay down your tools. A drought is coming
The colony heard no real promise.
Work stops so water can be hoarded.

All cheered as they got their full rations of water.
For some it has been months since a proper drink.
Some may have gotten carried away and drunk more than they should have.
But at least everyone is happy
A rare proper drink puts a spring in every step.

Water was scarce, the sole source of life in this dead world, and it was our job to secure as much of it as possible.
As {CP_Speaker_Name} grabbed her canteen during work, she prepared to silence the thirst even a little.
It was empty.
They sigh. It would not be until the next day that they get new rations.

For the first time since we arrived, we could see the bottom of the now-shallow river.
And right there in the mud lay a crate.
One could only imagine what would be inside.
Soaked research documents, almost all stained and unreadable
Old metal parts, most of it rusted
A bunch of bottles containing a mystery fluid
Rotten food. Well, at least the crate is in good shape

We can't believe our eyes. We are not the only ones.
Early in the morning a group of beavers arrived. Nobody recognized them. They are not from our town.
What should we do with them?
Take them all in. We need all the paws we can get
[[C]][[+]]+{I1} Adult Beaver +{I2} [[icon:UI/images/game/ico-child]] Child Beaver [[-]]Contamination and injuries among the arrivals

Dehydrated, sick, and injured, all were welcomed and scheduled for treatment.
Their representative, a young male, approached you with a key.
"With this key I trust you with my family and our resources. Please guide and protect them."

You sit in the city center with little left to do. The paperwork for so few healthy arrivals did not take long.
Then shouting: "You beavers are monsters. You sent my family to die."
The only healthy adult of the new group is fighting the builders. You rush down, too slow. He is on the ground with a hammer near him.
I guess I have paperwork to shred
[[C]][[-]]One beaver dies. One beaver is injured
{0} died in a fight over the refused refugees.

You aren't just a leader. You are part of the workforce, and you help wherever you can.
But your leadership duties keep growing, leaving you inefficient in the field.
Regardless, it is what I have to do
Paperwork pulls paws off the tools.

You were personally helping in the very beginning.
Recently that has become the niche part of your job.
Each day brings more decisions than the last. You'd like to complain, but it is definitely more relaxed than working your back away.
You lean back in your chair, taking a sip of water while looking at some schematics
{0} died while the captain sat with the schematics.

You try not to fall asleep reading a letter of another beaver's concerns.
Face-to-face meetings took too long, so you switched to a suggestion box.
The workday ends. You skipped lunch. Your stomach growls, your eyes strain, and the unopened pile is still there.

When we arrived, things were simple. Few beavers, simple problems.
As the colony grows, more issues pop up than one beaver can handle.
"I don't want to die" became "my dwelling doesn't have enough windows."
Every small concern lands on your shoulders. Your days are reading and answering letters.

The colony needs some kind of government.
The ones you travelled with want the old town's way: the elderly and wisest elected to rule together, leaving you the important tasks.
The foreigner minority fear exclusion. They want every beaver to have a say, whoever they are.
The young, traumatized by this world, fear a popularity contest. They would rather you pick a few individuals to help, and keep the squabbling down.
[[C]]A council of the old and wise. [[-]]{%1} life expectancy for [[time:{F3}d]]. Bureaucratic nightmare is removed.
[[C]]A council of representatives. [[-]]{%2} working speed for [[time:{F3}d]]. Bureaucratic nightmare is removed.
I will not leave my duties to those I don't trust
[[C]]Pay [[good:Science:{I1}]] in [[time:{F4}d]]. A council of those you choose.
The old ways are heavy on the longest-lived.
Everyone has a say, and work slows for it.
